name: Hyrum Smith
role: Joseph Smith’s older brother, Church patriarch and Assistant President
dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, named patriarch in the January 1841 revelation, and killed with Joseph at Carthage on 27 June 1844.
importance: Section 11 answers his wish to help in May 1829 by telling him to prepare before he preaches. In Kirtland he was named to the committee to build the Lord’s house (sections 94–95). He shared Liberty Jail with Joseph in 1838–1839. Section 124 praises his integrity and makes him patriarch, and section 135 reports his death beside Joseph.
connections: He was the son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and an older brother of Joseph and Samuel H. Smith. He worked with Reynolds Cahoon and Jared Carter on the Kirtland building committee and was the father of Joseph F. Smith.

sources.title: Hyrum Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP biography: born 9 Feb. 1800, Tunbridge, Vermont; baptized June 1829; one of the Eight Witnesses; counselor in First Presidency 1837; succeeded his father as patriarch (JSP says 1840; D&C 124 of Jan. 1841 appoints him). Death date on the JSP page was cut off but matches 27 June 1844 in D&C 135. “Hyrum” alone refers only to him in the text.
